newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up as overseas funds return.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up as overseas funds return.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended higher on Friday with funds seen flowing back into the market from abroad and much of the demand focused on Shanghai Chlor-Alkali Chemical, brokers said.
Domestic institutions turned their attention to index heavyweight Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development, which also helped to boost the index, they said.
The B index put on 0.887 point or 1.22 percent to 73.790 on volume of 9.242 million shares worth $3.93 million, compared with 10.321 million shares on Thursday.

Shanghai Chlor Alkali was the second most actively traded stock on heavy isntitutional buying due to market talk of restructuring, brokers said. It rose $0.008 or 3.39 percent to $0.244 on volume of 822,500 shares.
Market leader Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone also was strong, gaining $0.036 or 2.91 percent to $1,270 on volume of 811,600 shares.
Brokers said selective buying by institutions supported the market but volume was limited as retail investors kept to the sidelines.
Brokers said funds were flowing into the market from Hong Kong after recent strong advances took the Hang Seng Index to record levels.
"Some of the hot money has begun to flow back to the B share market as the upward potential for H shares traded in Hong Kong may be limited after the recent gains," one broker said.
"If institutions continue to support the market, more follow-through demand will emerge early next week and the index will rise further in the short term," another broker said.
Of the 45 B share issues, 39 were traded, with 25 of them gaining ground. Twelve were lower with two unchanged.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi rose $0.014 to $0.834 after it reported a 52.7 percent rise in first-half profits. It linked the rise to an expanded taxi and bus fleet.
Shanghai Narcissus Electric Appliances was the day's star performer on a technical rebound, jumping $0.008 or 6.66 percent to $0.128 on volume of 22,000 shares.

Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor was the most actively traded issue on insitutional selling amid concerns about its interim results. It lost $0.008 or 2.01 percent to $0.390 on volume of 997,200 shares.
Shanghai's A share index ended slightly firmer with most investors cautious ahead of the weekend after solid gains over the past few days, brokers said.
The index inched up 2.897 points or 0.23 percent to 1,248.475 points on volume of 305.7 million shares worth 3.1 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index slipped 18.391 points or 0.49 percent to 3,742.935 points.
Dali Paper was the best A share performer on talk that it will post solid interim results. It surged 1.16 yuan or 10.01 percent to 12.74 yuan on volume of 862,400 shares.
